item_verdicts.durability: The new surface is falsifiable in both directions and shown so by mutation. Removing the note at its source in _rerank_dd_hits (return `ordered, None`) reds test_skipped_rerank_leaves_the_note_in_summary_and_report (1 failed, 15 passed, EXIT=1) — reproduced independently here at 54c5a3f66. A second, distinct mutation this review applied — deleting the formatter's note-print block from format_search_dd_report — reds the same test (1 failed, EXIT=1), so both halves of the surface (summary propagation and report rendering) carry a guard that fires. The inverse is held by test_completed_rerank_leaves_no_note, which pins that a completed rerank leaves neither the summary key nor an `Rerank:` line in the report. Marked just short of perfect because the skipped-path test asserts presence and propagation only, not the note's wording (a deliberate ownership boundary, documented in the manifest and the test docstring), and the read-only/DD-only zero-call tests assert call counts on a separately-constructed tool rather than driving the server object end to end.

The note is the string the shared owner rerank_candidates (imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:171, used by both code and wiki search) already returns; _rerank_dd_hits stops discarding it, the summary carries it under the key the plan names (rerank_note), and format_search_dd_report prints it beneath the hits exactly where the plan says.
